The likely fault is in [ssh.py](/app/lib/ansible/plugins/connection/ssh.py:1332): Windows stderr is parsed only when it starts with `#< CLIXML`. Passing the whole stream to `_parse_clixml` would also lose surrounding text. The replacement should isolate each complete CLIXML block, parse it, and preserve all bytes before and after it.

In [powershell.py](/app/lib/ansible/plugins/shell/powershell.py:31), the escape regex accepts arbitrary combinations of zero and hex bytes instead of four UTF-16-BE zero/hex pairs. I reproduced a `ValueError` for the valid literal `_x\u6100\u6200\u6300\u6400_`. The parser also returns empty bytes for an incomplete block and raises `ParseError` for malformed XML, so the new helper should retain those blocks unchanged and apply UTF-8 decoding with cp437 fallback to complete blocks.

Existing [parser tests](/app/test/units/plugins/shell/test_powershell.py:8) cover complete CLIXML but not mixed stderr, incomplete blocks, or cp437. I recorded the findings in `.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md`. **No project source or tests were changed** because this role is limited to fault localization.

Implemented CLIXML replacement for Windows SSH stderr. Complete blocks are decoded and replaced while surrounding bytes and invalid or incomplete blocks are preserved. The escape regex now matches UTF-16-BE sequences correctly, and the helper falls back to cp437 when UTF-8 decoding fails.

Added coverage for mixed, multiline, repeated, empty, malformed, and cp437 input. All 46 relevant PowerShell and SSH unit tests pass; `git diff --check` passes.

The existing PowerShell and SSH tests pass: `PYTHONPATH=lib python -m pytest -q test/units/plugins/shell/test_powershell.py test/units/plugins/connection/test_ssh.py` → **46 passed**.

A correctness defect remains in [powershell.py](/app/lib/ansible/plugins/shell/powershell.py:122): the helper groups adjacent `<Objs>` elements before parsing. I reproduced a valid element followed by a malformed closed element; the helper returned the entire raw CLIXML input, losing the valid element’s decoded text. Parse adjacent elements separately so the valid text is replaced and the malformed element stays unchanged.

Fixed CLIXML replacement so adjacent `<Objs>` elements are parsed independently. A malformed element now stays unchanged without preventing a valid neighbor from being decoded. Added a regression test for that case.
